section_summary: This section concerns American holdings of Japanese municipal bonds and shares, with most pages devoted to Ujigawa Electric Power Company dollar bonds. A 1947 despatch encloses a detailed report on the bonds’ wartime conversion, unpaid interest, Japanese government assumption of liability, and cancelled mortgage. The report is followed by translated Japanese laws, finance orders, and a list of outstanding bond numbers.

subfiles.title: Department of State charge slip
subfiles.about: Records the charge of a bondholders file.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip for a file concerning bondholders.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning City of Yokohama bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains the Department’s position on an American client’s three City of Yokohama bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department describes foreign securities as private investments, suggests contacting the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and invites the holder to submit bond and citizenship details. It cannot yet say what a peace treaty or claims process will provide.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about City of Yokohama External Loan bonds
subfiles.about: Asks whether a client can recover on three City of Yokohama External Loan of 1926 bonds.
subfiles.summary: Prendergast asks about recovery through Japanese reparations, the Alien Property Custodian, or another source.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about reported sale of Japanese shares
subfiles.about: Requests the directive behind a newspaper statement about foreigners acquiring Japanese shares.
subfiles.summary: Korb asks whether the reported change to share trading rules rests on an official directive.

subfiles.title: Japanese Shares Will Be Sold Soon
subfiles.about: Reports plans to sell Japanese company shares to the public.
subfiles.summary: The article discusses share pricing, public ownership, and the government’s hope that sales will curb inflation.

subfiles.title: Reply to Samuel Korb on Japanese securities
subfiles.about: Responds to Korb’s inquiry about the sale of Japanese securities.
subfiles.summary: Whitman encloses press releases on Japanese securities and the resumption of international trade.

subfiles.title: Allied National Interests in Ujigawa Denki Kabushiki Kaisha
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on Allied holdings of Ujigawa Electric Power Company bonds.
subfiles.summary: The despatch recommends sending the bank the enclosed report and property protection instructions. It notes a moratorium on limitation periods and says procedures for adjudicating losses against Japan have not been established.

subfiles.title: Report on Status of Ujigawa Electric Power Company First Mortgage 7% Sinking Fund Gold Bonds
subfiles.from: Industrial Bank of Japan, Foreign Business Department
subfiles.about: Details the status of Ujigawa dollar bonds after wartime reorganization and bond conversion.
subfiles.summary: The report traces Ujigawa’s absorption into Kansai Electric Supply Company, sinking fund and interest payments, conversion of Japanese-held bonds, and the Japanese government’s assumption of the remaining $864,000 in bonds presumed held by Allied nationals. It explains that the original mortgage was cancelled under wartime law and supplies financial exhibits and an annex list.

subfiles.title: List of annexes to the Ujigawa bond report
subfiles.about: Identifies the nine annexes accompanying the bond report.
subfiles.summary: Lists laws, bond numbers, finance orders, statements, property records, and reparations materials.

subfiles.title: Electric Power Distribution Control Ordinance
subfiles.about: Sets the rules for organizing regional electric distribution companies.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance authorizes the government to designate companies, transfer electric facilities, and establish distribution companies. Its provisions address assets, debts, mortgages, shares, registration, taxes, management, and official supervision, providing the legal basis for Ujigawa’s reorganization.

subfiles.title: Law Relating to the Treatment of the Foreign Bonds
subfiles.about: Provides for wartime conversion of foreign bonds and government assumption of unconverted obligations.
subfiles.summary: The law permits conversion of specified foreign bonds into yen bonds and authorizes the Japanese government to assume obligations on bonds left unconverted. It voids mortgages and other original contractual effects associated with those assumed bonds, while retaining principal and interest obligations.

subfiles.title: List of Numbers of the Outstanding Bonds
subfiles.about: Lists outstanding Ujigawa Electric Power Company bond numbers.
subfiles.summary: The annex enumerates bond numbers and ends with a subtotal of 773 bonds at $1,000 each.

subfiles.title: Finance order on payment of foreign-currency bond interest
subfiles.about: Orders payment in Japan of interest on sterling and United States dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: The order requires interest payments in Japanese currency from January 1942 at official exchange rates.

subfiles.title: Finance order on hostile nationals’ blocked interest accounts
subfiles.about: Directs payment of certain bond interest into a designated hostile nationals’ blocked account.
subfiles.summary: The order describes deposits at the Yokohama Specie Bank, exchange-rate calculations, and repayments when coupons or certified claims are paid elsewhere. An attached note defines the interest amounts covered.

subfiles.title: Hostile Nationals’ Property Control Law
subfiles.about: Regulates custody and disposal of property belonging to hostile nationals.
subfiles.summary: The law empowers the government to appoint custodians, direct payments and property transfers, void unauthorized transactions, and penalize interference. Its discharge provision bears on wartime payments of bond interest.

subfiles.title: Annex VI divider
subfiles.about: Marks the beginning of the next annex.
subfiles.summary: Title page for Annex VI; its contents follow outside this section.
